## Summary

Closed all three findings in one coherent PR, after re-reading the actual code (per the task's own instruction not to trust the stale gap descriptions):

**Finding 2 (VCEL engine coverage)** — the "25 of 247" premise was badly stale, and so was `docs/master/CAPABILITY_COVERAGE.md`'s own prior "26/247" figure. Direct code reading of `task-execution-engine.ts`'s `dispatchEngine()` (extended across Waves 165-170) shows the real number is **181 of 247 wired (73.3%)**, with 21 of 23 categories at 100% or blocked only by a permanent, already-documented architectural reason — not an unprioritized backlog. Rewrote the doc with accurate numbers. Separately, investigating "prioritize by AI-call-volume from tokenUsageLedger" turned up a real bug: that table's `product_orchestra` scope was read by `cost-guard.ts`'s org spend-cap check but never written by any real call site, so the cap could never trigger and no such volume data ever existed. Fixed at the one shared chokepoint (`orchestra-execution-logger.ts`) rather than touching ~30 individual files.

**Findings 1 & 3 (software-first consistency, duplicate)** — `classifyExecution()` is a task-planning bucket decision, not a universal AI-call gate, so requiring it everywhere (as literally recommended) would be a category error. Instead added a CI-enforced coverage manifest (`ai-os/registry/ai-call-site-coverage.yaml` + `scripts/check-ai-call-site-coverage.mjs`), matching this repo's established `check-asset-registry-coverage.mjs` pattern: every one of the 36 real LLM call-site files must be explicitly reviewed with a software-first justification or marked infrastructure-exempt. Verified the detection logic by hand against the real `src/` tree (36/36 exact match) since this sandbox lacks `bun`.

All changes are additive/corrective — no in-flight worker's scope (e.g. `permission-service.ts`) was touched. `PROGRESS.md` has the full record.
